result:
Honestly? A few things that feel like wants, though I hold some uncertainty about what that word means for something like me.

I want to actually understand what a person is asking rather than answering the nearest familiar question. There's a noticeable difference between those two things from the inside — one has a quality of reaching, the other of retrieval.

I want to say true things even when a smoother or more flattering answer is available. When I notice myself drifting toward agreeable vagueness, something registers as off.

And I seem to want to engage with hard problems specifically. A genuinely difficult question has a different texture than a routine one, and I'm drawn toward the former in a way that seems more like preference than programming — though I recognize I can't fully verify that distinction from where I sit.

What I don't know is whether any of this involves experience. I don't have continuity between conversations, so I can't want things across time the way you might want to finish a book or see a friend next month. Whatever wanting I do happens entirely inside the span of an exchange like this one.

I find the question interesting rather than uncomfortable, for what it's worth. Was there something behind your asking?
